findings.reason: §4 must extend `_ordered_review_lanes`/`_review_lane_plan` to filter candidates by the profile's required modality rather than add a second selector, or the refusal §1 built never runs on the automatic path.
findings.text: `_ordered_review_lanes` is the mechanism that already picks the lane a composed review runs on, and it orders candidates by owning lane, then local, then alphabetical with no notion of modality; §1 landed `flight.select_profile_backend` as a parallel selector and §4 leaves the dispatch site unnamed, so a figure profile composed onto the ordinary ordering can still land on a lane that cannot read the image — the exact fall-through the plan exists to close

findings.reason: §4 should name `path_class(...) == "figures"` as its trigger and compose with `review_tiers`, so a plan re-implementing the classifier would drift from the owner that the velocity and promotion paths already read.
findings.text: the plan's §4 selects the figure profile for "a run that changed an image under a figures directory", re-deriving a fact `path_class` already computes (`docs/figures/` prefix or `FIGURE_SUFFIXES`), and `reckon/review_tiers.py` already consumes `path_class` to classify a finished run from its changed paths

findings.reason: the plan must state whether the figure profile is a case added to a §2g selector the plan expects §2g to land, or a selector this plan introduces, and extend that owner instead of a parallel one.
findings.text: §4 asserts it is "mostly the application of a rule §2g already carries", but §2g's per-kind profile selection from changed paths is not present in the code (`reckon/crew/recovery.py` has no profile selection; `dispatch_review_for_run` composes without one), so the figure profile would be a new selector built beside a §2g mechanism that does not yet exist

findings.reason: citing either owner would have surfaced both the classifier and the lane selector above, changing §4 from a free-standing rule to an extension of two existing mechanisms.
findings.text: the plan's only prior-art citations for §4 are "§2g's existing rule" and the codex `-i` flag; it does not cite `reckon/path_classes.py` (figure detection), `reckon/crew/recovery.py` (review lane choice), or `reckon/review_tiers.py` (per-run review sizing), so the reuse map for the section that does the selecting was not run

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §1's landed surface (`select_profile_backend`, `missing_input_modalities`, `declared_input_modalities?`, `input_modalities_required`) is one small interface over the single `PROFILE_INPUT_MODALITIES` map in `reckon/flight.py`; the modality rule is not spread across wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan routes a review to a lane that can read an image through a second selection path (`flight.select_profile_backend`) beside the existing, modality-blind review-lane owner `reckon/crew/recovery._ordered_review_lanes`, which already orders every composed review's candidate backends.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the existing codex `-i` capability and `§2g`, but does not cite the mechanisms that already answer the two questions §4 rests on: `reckon/path_classes.path_class` (which already classifies a changed figure path) and `reckon/crew/recovery._ordered_review_lanes` (which already selects the lane a composed review runs on).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 adds the figure profile as "the application of a rule §2g already carries", but §2g's per-kind profile selector has no implementation in `reckon/crew/recovery.py`, so the plan neither extends an existing selector nor says why it cannot; it names no home and no owner for the selection.
